title: SceneCOT: Eliciting Grounded Chain-of-Thought Reasoning in 3D Scenes
claim: A complex grounded question is answered by an explicit step-by-step reasoning chain that localizes the target object and retrieves visual evidence.
layout: 2 panels, left question and 3D scene, right reasoning trace, red arrows linking
description: Two rounded panels side by side. The left panel has a light blue speech box with a situated question: 'I am facing a desk. There is a brown chair on my left. What is the color of the bike on my 2 o'clock.' Below it is a top-down textured 3D room scan. A small red box marks the bike's location in the scene. The right panel is headed 'Thinking...' and shows a gray structured trace in XML-like tags: think_type (attribute question), grd_rgn, think_rgn, think_grd, an [OBJ] token, think_task, highlight_obj, an image of a bicycle between img_start and img_end, think_sum, and finally answer 'silver'. Two bold red arrows run from the red box in the scene. One points to the [OBJ] token and the other to the retrieved bike photo. The eye goes first to the red arrows and the scene.
caption: Reasoning chain visualization of \model. Example of how \model decomposes a 3D question into step-by-step reasoning: from identifying the task type, localizing relevant objects, and grounding the target entity, to retrieving the visual clue and generating the final answer.
abstract: Existing research on 3D Large Language Models (LLMs) still struggles to achieve grounded question-answering, primarily due to the under-exploration of the mechanism of human-like scene-object grounded reasoning. This paper bridges the gap by presenting a novel framework. We first introduce a grounded Chain-of-Thought reasoning method in 3D scenes (SCENECOT), decoupling a complex reasoning task into simpler and manageable problems, and building corresponding visual clues based on multimodal expert modules. To enable such a method, we develop SCENECOT-185K, the first large-scale grounded CoT reasoning dataset, consisting of 185K high-quality instances. Extensive experiments across various complex 3D scene reasoning benchmarks demonstrate that our new framework achieves strong performance with high grounding-QA coherence. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first successful application of CoT reasoning to 3D scene understanding, enabling step-by-step human-like reasoning and showing potential for extension to broader 3D scene understanding scenarios.
